To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a sequence of plinian tuffs was erupted in the central Yukon region during the Late Cretaceous and early Paleocene, and that (ii) the eruption products have been transported and deposited over a wide area in northern Canada.
the Summit Creek tuff is the result of a series of plinian eruption events and that the nearest known source is located in the southern Yukon.

(1) the tuff beds were formed by fallout from plinian and/or ultraplinian eruption columns; (2) the source vent(s) are located in the central Yukon area; and (3) the eruption(s) took place in the Late Cretaceous–Early Tertiary, probably in the Paleocene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a possible plinian eruption of Paleocene age, which may represent an example of a large, high altitude, explosive eruption in the early Tertiary.
the recognition of plinian tuff deposits in the geologic record and with their interpretation as evidence for the occurrence of explosive eruptions of great magnitude.
the recognition of volcanic ash deposits and the reconstruction of the eruptive events which produced them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Summit Creek tuffs are plinian or ultraplinian in origin.
the tuff beds in the Summit Creek Formation represent a series of plinian eruption–deposition events, and that the source area was in central Yukon.
the Summit Creek Formation tuffs represent plinian or ultraplinian ashfall deposits of Paleocene age, and that their source vents lie in the central Yukon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tuffs are products of one or more plinian eruption(s) that occurred during the Paleocene, in an area that is presently the Yukon Territory.

the Summit Creek tuffs are the result of one or several large, high-altitude eruptions of the type that have been observed at geologically recent times, and that the eruptions occurred in central Yukon.
the Summit Creek Formation contains evidence for at least one and possibly several large plinian eruption(s) in central Yukon during Paleocene time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plinian eruption is a plausible mode of eruption for the Paleocene volcanism in the Yukon, and that the Summit Creek Formation is a potential record of such eruptions.
the plinian eruption style was present at least since the Late Paleocene in central Yukon.
there is no reason to think that the eruption of the Summit Creek tuff was any more or less violent than any modern plinian eruption.
